summary: Nipomo sprawls across 15 square miles of rolling mesa between the Santa Maria Valley and the Pacific, yet its population density — just 1,143 per square mile — means much of that land is still open agricultural fields, eucalyptus windrows, and sandy hillside scrub, giving the unincorporated community an unmistakably rural-suburban pacing rare for coastal California. The Nipomo Dunes complex, one of the largest remaining coastal dune ecosystems in the state, sits just minutes to the west, and the buried set of Cecil B. DeMille's 1923 *Ten Commandments* still lies beneath those sands — a genuinely strange archaeological footnote. With a median home value of $674,100 against a median household income of $102,382, the price-to-income ratio lands around 6.6:1 — steep, but notably lower than neighboring San Luis Obispo, making it function largely as a bedroom community for jobs in SLO, Santa Maria, and Vandenberg Space Force Base. Daily highs average a remarkably mild 71°F year-round with over nine hours of sunshine, though marine-layer fog regularly blankets mornings. Dining and retail remain thin — a few local spots along Thompson Road, no real downtown grid — so errands often mean a car trip north or south. Nipomo offers the quiet of agricultural space at a coastal-adjacent price, with the tradeoff being that nearly everything beyond groceries requires a drive.
